idiom_name: narrowest-owner placement ladder: local/component state, closest common parent, scoped provider, global store
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: declare a piece of state in the smallest unit that uses it and treat every move upwards as a deliberate promotion. Apply the decision procedure per value — used only where it is declared, leave it there; used by one child, colocate it in that child; used by a sibling or an ancestor, lift it to the closest common parent and pass the value down with an updater callback up; used across distant subtrees, place a scoped provider or state container as low as the shared consumers allow; genuinely global and long-lived, give it to the store. Do not duplicate a value to avoid a promotion, and do not promote a value to avoid thinking about its owner. Persistence and cross-cutting observation (URL, telemetry, undo) are deliberate additions, not defaults.
code_sketch:
state = newCell(initial)
# only the declaring component reads it -> stop
# a child needs it          -> move the cell down into the child
# a sibling needs it        -> move the cell to the closest common parent
#                                value down, updater callback up
# distant consumers need it -> scoped provider, mounted as low as they allow
# global + long-lived       -> store (session, server cache, cross-route data)
pitfalls: Promoting a value out of habit (root or store by default) recreates the over-lifted state the pattern exists to remove; promote only for a named second consumer.
Colocating two copies of the same logical value makes them drift; one owner plus derived values beats duplicated ownership.
Forgetting lifetime: state that must survive remounting or navigation is not saveable by colocation alone — pair it with the runtime's persistence mechanism.
Forgetting that the decision procedure runs continuously: as the component tree changes, previously colocated state may need to be lifted or moved to a provider.
Promoting state to a global store for 'consistency' when the value is only read by one feature — this is premature globalization.

Wrong move: declaring a value where the data arrives (screen root, query result, route loader) instead of where it is read -> the whole subtree above the reader re-renders on every change and the owner is untraceable -> push the value down into the reading component (or derive it there) and lift only for a named second consumer.

Wrong move: reflexively making every mutable browser-native value a component cell (current URL in useState, media playback time, open dialog) -> state desynchronises from history/back-button behaviour and must be re-synced by hand -> let the browser own it (URL parameters, media elements) and read it where displayed.
